# Stay Eego (스테이 이고)

> An hour from Seoul, a two-storey home over forty years old below Suwon Hwaseong Fortress. Just two guest rooms downstairs, and a warm Korean breakfast cooked by the host couple every morning.

A two-room homestay in Haenggung-dong, Suwon, South Korea, run by the couple who live upstairs. Bookings and payment go through Airbnb. This file is a plain-text summary of the site for language models; the pages below are the source.

## At a glance

- Name: Stay Eego (스테이 이고)
- Address: 123-16 Sinpung-dong, Paldal-gu, Suwon, Gyeonggi-do (경기도 수원시 팔달구 신풍동 123-16)
- Where: Haenggung-dong, Suwon
- From Seoul: One hour
- Rooms: Two, with private bathrooms
- Breakfast: Included in your stay
- Room names: Alleyway room, Garden room
- Each room: One queen bed, up to 2 guests; Private toilet and shower
- Check-in and check-out: Check-in is from 4 pm, and check-out is by 11 am.
- Languages: We chat comfortably in Korean and English, and we also speak a little Japanese.
- Booking: All bookings and payments go through Airbnb. Choose your open dates on this site or press a booking button and we’ll take you straight to Stay Eego’s Airbnb page.
- Guest rating: Rated 4.99 for the Garden room and 4.98 for the Alleyway room on Airbnb, with 388 reviews so far.

## The house

Nene’s family has lived in this house for more than forty years, since her grandfather’s time. Nene was born and raised in this neighbourhood, and Minho fell for Haenggung-dong fifteen years ago and opened a guesthouse here.
After we married, we ran a small restaurant on the ground floor for several years. Now we keep just two guest rooms. Because no more than two sets of guests ever stay at once, we have the time to chat with you and cook a proper breakfast each morning.
The two of us live right upstairs. Whenever you need a hand we’re right nearby, and when you’re resting in your room we’ll quietly stay out of the way.

## Rooms

Two rooms sit side by side on the ground floor: Alleyway and Garden. Both have wide windows and a private bathroom, with solid-wood beds and furniture built to fit each room.
- Alleyway room: A wide window opens onto a Haenggung-dong lane. Looking out over the neighbours’ earthenware jars and low tiled roofs, you can lie back in bed and watch the quiet rhythm of the neighbourhood from morning to night. Deep green walls, warm cherry-wood furniture and soft orange lighting give the room a calm, settled feel. A private toilet and shower booth are right inside the room.
- Garden room: A large picture window looks out onto the front garden. Lie in bed and the window fills with trees and sky, and in the daytime the room is bright and cosy with sunlight. Deep green walls, cherry-wood furniture and warm orange lighting make it an easy place for your eyes and mind to rest. A private toilet and shower booth are right inside the room.
- In each room: One queen bed, up to 2 guests; Private toilet and shower; Air conditioning and heated floors; Towels, hairdryer, shampoo and body wash; Lock on the room door; Breakfast included

## Shared space and breakfast

Step outside your room and you’re in the ground-floor lounge shared by both rooms. We serve breakfast here at the long wooden table every morning, and during the day or evening you can sit with a cup of tea or a book.
The kitchen at the back is where we prepare breakfast, so we don’t open it to guests. Anytime you’re having fruit or need glasses, plates or cutlery, just ask and we’ll set them out at your table right away.
Every morning in our kitchen we cook a neat Korean breakfast of warm rice and soup, a fluffy rolled omelette hot from the pan, and seasonal namul (seasoned vegetables). Breakfast is included with every stay.
If you don’t eat spicy food or have any ingredients to avoid, please let us know before check-in so we can prepare a meal that’s easy on you.

## Cats

Neighbourhood cats drop by the garden all day to nap, and our own cat Siru lives indoors. Plenty of guests end up spending the whole day sitting by their window just watching the garden cats.
If you have a cat allergy, please keep this in mind and let us know before booking.

## Neighbourhood

Step out the gate and the walking path along Suwon Hwaseong Fortress (수원화성) is just ahead, with decades-old local restaurants and independent cafés tucked into every lane within easy walking distance.
When you check in, we first ask what kinds of food and atmosphere you like, then pick out walking routes and places to eat that suit the day’s weather and your taste. We’ve also put together a map of 29 neighbourhood spots the two of us go to regularly.

## Getting here

Address: 123-16 Sinpung-dong, Paldal-gu, Suwon, Gyeonggi-do (경기도 수원시 팔달구 신풍동 123-16)
- From Seoul Station: Take the train to Suwon Station and transfer to a taxi — it takes just over an hour to our front door. About 30 km in a straight line.
- From Gangnam Station: Take a Suwon-bound express bus from Gangnam Station and you’ll reach the neighbourhood in about an hour without transfers. About 24 km in a straight line.
- From Incheon Airport: Take the Suwon-bound airport limousine bus and transfer to a taxi at Suwon Station — it takes about two hours to the house.
- By car: You can park right in front of the house. Just let us know before you set off so we can keep the space clear for you.

## Common questions

- Do we stay in the same house as the hosts? Yes. The two of us live upstairs on the second floor, and both guest rooms are on the ground floor. Each room and its bathroom are completely private to you, while the central lounge on the ground floor is shared by the two rooms. Only we use the kitchen to prepare breakfast, but whenever you need plates, cups or cutlery, just ask and we’ll bring them right out.
- What languages can we communicate in? We chat comfortably in Korean and English, and we also speak a little Japanese.
- What time are check-in and check-out? Check-in is from 4 pm, and check-out is by 11 am.
- Can we do laundry during our stay? Yes — if you need laundry done, we’re happy to wash and dry your clothes free of charge. Just let us know.
- How do we book and pay? All bookings and payments go through Airbnb. Choose your open dates on this site or press a booking button and we’ll take you straight to Stay Eego’s Airbnb page.
